title: Timeout worker does not inherit MLflow thread-local state such as the active run (open review concern)
answers: why does log_metric inside a scorer create a separate run
why does a scorer see no active run when timeout is set
is the active run visible inside a scorer with a timeout
body:
Symptom: a scorer with a timeout runs under mlflow.start_run() but sees no active run, and mlflow.log_metric() inside it may create a separate run. The same scorer with timeout=None works.
Root cause: Scorer._run_with_timeout uses copy_context(), which copies only ContextVar values. MLflow's active run and active model are stored in ThreadLocalVariable, which the copied context does not carry into the daemon worker thread.
Fix pattern: a review comment asks to copy the relevant ThreadLocalVariable values into the worker explicitly. The diff as shown does not do this, so treat it as an open gap.
Constraints: any change that moves scorer execution into another thread must preserve active run and active model. Check this with a scorer that calls log_metric under an active run.
applies: Changes to how scorers are dispatched to threads, or to ThreadLocalVariable-based MLflow state used during evaluation.
says: Evaluation metrics with a timeout create unwanted separate experiment runs when recording metrics.
Setting an evaluation timeout causes the evaluator to lose track of the active experiment run.
Metrics logged during timed evaluation end up in a different experiment run instead of current.
Ensure timed evaluation tasks preserve the current active experiment run when recording evaluation results.
search: Scorer execution with a timeout fails to inherit MLflow thread-local state, causing workers to lose the active run and active model. In mlflow/genai/scorers/base.py:Scorer._run_with_timeout, copy_context() copies only ContextVar values rather than ThreadLocalVariable state into the daemon worker thread. This causes scorers with timeouts to see no active run and potentially create a separate run when calling mlflow.log_metric(). Applies to scorer thread dispatching and evaluation state changes, leaving explicit copying of ThreadLocalVariable values as an open review gap.
